entries.output:
# acme-demos

Interactive product demos, built with `interactive-demo`.

Each folder under `demos/` is one demo: a `demo.config.json` describing
the steps, and the screenshots and recordings it references under
`assets/`. The project itself is configured by `interactive-demo.json`.

```bash
npm install
```

## Record your product

Needs Google Chrome.

```bash
npx interactive-demo capture start https://app.example.com
# click through the product in the window that opens
npx interactive-demo capture stop
```

Every click becomes a step, with the pointer where you clicked. `stop`
writes the recording as a new demo under `demos/`.

## Preview and edit

```bash
npm run dev
```

Opens a local preview of every demo, with the editor at `/__demo/editor/`.
Edits are written straight to the files in this folder.

## Ship it

```bash
npx interactive-demo login && npx interactive-demo publish
```

Puts the demo online and prints its link. Publishing again updates the same
link, so embeds keep working. Once the project has more than one demo, name
it: `npx interactive-demo publish demos/<slug>`. `npx interactive-demo embed`
prints the embed snippet.

## Host it yourself instead

```bash
npm run build
```

Writes a self-contained static folder per demo under `dist/`. Deploy it to
any static host; the build prints the embed snippets, which are the same as
the published ones apart from the host.

entries.text:
I made the onboarding demo. It's local only: nothing was published and I didn't log in.

**What it covers.** I couldn't find a dedicated onboarding page in the app, so I recorded the path through it that matches your activation funnel. It's 8 steps:

1. **Cover:** "Get Acme Analytics set up in under two minutes"
2. **Overview:** click "New funnel"
3. **Activation funnel:** click "Save funnel"
4. **Segments:** click "New segment"
5. **Workspace settings:** click "Invite teammates"
6. **Invite modal:** click "Send invite" (zoomed in on the modal)
7. **Back on Overview:** the KPI cards are highlighted with a "That's onboarding done" message
8. **Closing screen:** "Your workspace is ready", with a Replay button

Each step's "Click on X" text from the recording is replaced with copy that says why you'd click it. The steps are grouped into three chapters: build your first funnel, save a segment, invite your team. The theme uses Acme's ink black and the app's system font. The screens are real screenshots of `http://localhost:4173/app/` at 1440×900. Validation passes with no errors or warnings, and I clicked through it in a browser to check that it renders.

**To preview it:**
```sh
cd acme-demos
npm run dev        # then open http://localhost:3000/onboarding/
```
You can edit the text in the browser editor at `/__demo/editor/`, or directly in `demos/onboarding/demo.config.json`. When you're ready to publish, run `npx interactive-demo login && npx interactive-demo publish demos/onboarding`.

**Things to check:**
- The demo header shows the project name "acme-demos". To show "Acme Analytics", change `brand.name` in `interactive-demo.json`. That setting applies to every demo in the project, so I didn't change it.
- If your real onboarding is a different flow, such as a signup wizard on another URL, tell me where it is and I'll record that one instead.

The recording browser and my preview server are both stopped. I left one `interactive-demo dev` server running on port 4731 because I didn't start it.

Files are in `acme-demos/`:
- `demos/onboarding/demo.config.json`
- `demos/onboarding/assets/screen-001.png` to `screen-006.png`
- `interactive-demo.json` (the demo was added to its list automatically)

widgets.title: Get Acme Analytics set up in under two minutes
widgets.description: Build your first funnel, save a segment and invite your team. Five clicks, all in the product.

annotations.text: Your workspace opens on **Overview**: active users, activation and revenue at a glance. Start onboarding by building your first funnel. Click **New funnel**.

steps.label: Start a funnel
steps.script: Overview is home base. From here, the first thing to set up is a funnel.

annotations.text: Acme maps the five activation steps from your events automatically, and flags the biggest drop-off for you. Looks right? Click **Save funnel**.

steps.label: Save the funnel
steps.script: The activation funnel shows where new users stall, from first visit to inviting a teammate.

annotations.text: Saved funnels feed **Segments**: reusable audiences like *Trial, day 3* or *Churn risk* that the whole team can use. Click **New segment**.

steps.label: Build a segment
steps.script: Segments turn the people in your funnel into audiences you can act on.

annotations.text: Your data sources are connected and syncing. The last onboarding step: bring your team in. Click **Invite teammates**.

steps.label: Invite your team
steps.script: Workspace settings hold members, seats and connected sources.

annotations.text: Add teammates by email and pick a role. Editors can build reports from day one. Click **Send invite**.

steps.label: Send the invite
steps.script: Invites land teammates in this same workspace, with the funnel and segments you just set up.

annotations.text: That's onboarding done. These numbers now track the funnel you built, and your teammates see the same view the moment they accept.

steps.label: You're set up
steps.script: Back on Overview, with a funnel, a segment and your team in place.

widgets.title: Your workspace is ready
widgets.description: Funnel saved, segment built, team invited. Now see where your users drop off.
